intro: This computer icon draws a desktop monitor with a bezel strip along the bottom of the screen, a short neck and a flat base. It means a desktop device or a large screen: use it for desktop app downloads, screen sharing, display settings, device lists and desktop preview modes in website and email builders.
meaning: A screen on a stand reads as a desktop computer, a fixed machine at a desk, which sets it apart from a laptop with a hinged keyboard and from a phone. In responsive design tools it sits in a row with phone and tablet icons, each meaning a preview width. People also read it as screen sharing or display options when it appears in a call or settings.
uses: Website builder toolbar: switches the canvas to a desktop preview width next to tablet and phone options.
Video call controls: starts screen sharing so others in the meeting can see your display.
Account security page: lists signed-in devices, with this glyph marking desktop browsers and apps.
Download page: points visitors to the Windows and Mac versions of the app beside mobile store links.
tips: In a device preview row, keep the monitor, tablet and phone glyphs at the same stroke weight and height so they read as one set.
For screen sharing, add an arrow or the label Share screen, because the plain monitor may suggest display settings instead.
Give each device toggle a clear accessible name, such as Desktop preview, so screen readers announce which width is selected.

faq.q: What is the difference between a monitor icon and a desktop icon?
faq.a: In most products they are the same glyph: a screen on a stand. Monitor tends to describe the hardware or display settings, while desktop describes the desktop version of an app or a desktop preview. The label you add decides which meaning people take.

faq.q: Which screen icon should a screen sharing button use?
faq.a: A monitor with an upward arrow, or the plain monitor with a Share screen label, is the clearest choice for sharing. Most video call apps use a variation of it, so people already know where to look for it in the call toolbar.
